readMe.a: Case Field Health & Tech Debt Analysis — XBU

readMe.b: Identify which Case fields are genuinely in use and which are tech debt, using measured record-level population rather than estimates.

Full re-measurement issued 2026-10-25. Every raw measure on Field Health was re-taken live from XBU production on 2026-10-25, replacing the 2026-08-27 read. The tab structure, column layout, Scoring Model inputs and every scored formula (Population through Effective Age) are carried over unchanged from the 2026-09-02 revision, so this workbook can be read side by side with the August XBU and September SBU workbooks.

Live Salesforce metadata (describe, FieldDefinition, Tooling CustomField and MetadataComponentDependency) read directly from XBU production (rainpos.my.salesforce.com) on 2026-10-25. No intermediate metadata export.

Not required. Created Date, Created By, Last Modified, Required?, Help Text and Description all come from the same live read. Required? = the field is not nillable. Created Date is the UTC date on the CustomField record; the Shipping_Address sub-fields take the compound parent's.
Live SOQL aggregates against XBU production (org 00D4W000008J2IAUA0, Rain Retail) on 2026-10-25. No record export. All measures are exact counts over every Case, not a sampled export.
2021-01-01 to 2026-10-25 (69 complete months plus 25 days of October 2026)

410 of 421 live Case fields assessed (Id excluded as a non-data field). The 11 Long Text Area fields cannot be filtered or aggregated in SOQL and are listed on Not Assessable. The 8 Shipping_Address sub-fields and the Shipping_Address__c parent ARE assessed; the parent counts a Case as populated when Street, City, Postal Code or State Code carries a value. Country Code is left out of that test because it defaults to US on most Cases. Since August, 31 Case fields have been deleted from the org and 12 added. See CHANGES SINCE THE AUGUST MEASUREMENT below.

Column "Age (days)", from the field's true Created Date. 49 fields (the standard fields) have no creation date in the metadata and show blank. Managed-package fields now carry their install date, which the August read left blank.
Column "% Populated (all records)" — measured across all 530,859 records, not sampled.

Columns "Eligible Records (since creation)" and "% Populated Since Creation" restrict the denominator to Cases created in or after the month the field was created (month-aligned, the same method as the SBU workbook). This is the fair measure: a field created in 2026 is not penalised for empty 2021 records.

"Adoption Lag (days)" is the gap between a field being created and the end of its first month of real use (>=1% of that month's cases). A long lag means the field sat unused after it was built; 4 fields waited over a year.
1 field(s) predate it and are measured across the whole window. Flagged in "Created Before Export Window".

68 fields are formulas or roll-up summaries. They compute a value on every record, so population, recency and trend are meaningless for them. Those three components score "n/a" and the total renormalises over information content, integration and documentation.

42 checkbox fields. A checkbox is populated on 100% of records by definition, so every measure here uses % TRUE instead — including recency and trend, which required a separate pass over the records for TRUE values.

readMe.a: 4. New fields sit outside the score ladder
readMe.b: Fields under the grace period are banded "Too New - Provisional" rather than given a Healthy/Retire rating, because two components are structurally biased against them: Trend compares a 90-day window that predates the field, and Integration/Documentation lag behind field creation. Their score still shows, but as advisory only. Fields are also banded Provisional if they have too few eligible records to measure, whatever their age.

One column carries provenance: Custom (348), Standard (49) or Managed Package (13). Managed-package fields belong to an installed app (ActOnIt, als_time, ringdna) and cannot be deleted at all, so they are excluded from Retire Candidates. The 7 ActOnIt fields are new since August.

Before the grace-period rule, SLA_Warning_Count__c — created 6 days before the export and populated on 100% of eligible cases — was banded "Likely Debt", purely because a brand-new formula field has not been added to layouts or documented yet. Trend now scores n/a for any field younger than the trend window, the same treatment formula fields get.

Columns "Source Records Populated" and "Variance vs Source" now compare the live count with the previous XBU measurement (Records Populated on the 2026-08-27 workbook). The two reads are 59 days apart, so this is an independent change-over-time check rather than the same-query consistency check of August. Variance vs Source is a live formula (Records Populated minus Source). 398 fields carry an August figure: 308 rose, 86 are unchanged and 4 fell (Time_Remaining__c, a formula, plus ContactFax, LastReferencedDate and LastViewedDate). The median change is +99. The 12 fields added since August show blank.
IsDeleted was not used to filter; the SOQL baseline excludes soft-deleted records by default.

Distinct values come from SOQL COUNT_DISTINCT over every Case. This replaces the 150-records-per-month sample used in August and matches the SBU method; the column is now headed "Distinct Values". Checkboxes show 1 when the box is ever TRUE and 0 when it never is. The 5 multi-select picklists and the Shipping_Address__c parent do not support COUNT_DISTINCT, so their distinct values were counted exactly by reading every populated record. A distinct count of 0 (37 fields) means the field is never populated.

The record measures cannot see external integrations. The live dependency crawl (MetadataComponentDependency) now also returns Report and Email Template references, counted under Other Refs, but it cannot see dashboards, list views or integration users. Standard fields are not covered by the dependency API and show 0 references. A field can look dead here and still break something on deletion.

"% Populated Last 90d" is the three most recent complete months (2026-07 to 2026-09) and "% Populated Last 365d" the twelve most recent complete months (2025-10 to 2026-09). The 25 days of October 2026 are excluded from both windows but included in the all-records and since-creation measures.
Every weight and threshold is an editable input (blue text, yellow fill). Change them and Field Health recalculates.
One row per assessed field: raw measures on the left, scored components and classification on the right.

47 hand-written per-field notes, carried over unchanged from the August workbook and shown alongside each field's current band, classification and action. 30 of the noted fields have since been deleted and are marked "Deleted from org".
Custom, non-required fields past the grace period with no measurable current value (46 fields, down from 79). Sorted by Total References, then Health Score.
Custom formula fields with no metadata references, or a single constant value.
Required fields not actually populated, fields adopted more than a year after creation, and fields with no help text or description.
A low score is a prompt to investigate, not an instruction to delete. Verify dependencies before removing any field.

"Effective Age (days)" (column AT) is now a live formula: the days between the Analysis as-of date (Scoring Model tab) and the older of the field's creation month and its first month carrying data. Formula and roll-up fields keep their metadata age, because they compute retroactively and would otherwise all look ancient; never-populated fields anchor to their creation month. It is reference information only: backfilled data can make a genuinely new field look years old, so the Band, Trend, Classification and Action formulas key the grace period on the literal "Age (days)" from the metadata Created Date. A field created within the grace period is always "Too New - Provisional" and can never be a retire candidate. The cost is that a deleted-and-redeployed long-standing field is parked provisional for one grace period — the safe direction of error.

31 Case fields were deleted from XBU production between 2026-08-27 and 2026-10-25: all 17 Zendesk_Support_Ticket_* fields, 11 other August retire candidates, and Dock__c, Ethernet_Cradle__c and P5_Terminal__c (required checkboxes noted "Retire/Delete" or "Check with Fulfillment Team"). 12 fields were added: 7 ActOnIt managed-package fields, Automation_Bypass__c, New_Processor__c, Original_Processor__c, Primary_Incident__c and Projected_Churn_Date__c. Of the August retire candidates, 51 remain in the org. CHECK: Case_Primary_Processor__c was deleted although its LH note reads "Field should not be deleted. Stores account primary processor".

Re-run the same live reads against XBU production (sf CLI login lhaigy@rainprod.com): describe + Tooling CustomField + MetadataComponentDependency for metadata; per-month SOQL COUNT aggregates batched 40 fields per query; a separate % TRUE pass per checkbox; exact COUNT_DISTINCT for cardinality; and month-aligned 90d/365d windows. Then set the Analysis as-of date on the Scoring Model tab.

Grace-period defect corrected: the "Too New" check previously read Effective Age, which backfilled data inflates, so fields created in mid-2026 (e.g. within the last 90 days) could be classed Retire candidate or Review. The check now reads actual Age (days). Classification and Action are now live formulas (with two new tunable thresholds on the Scoring Model tab) instead of static text, so they recalculate together with the scores. Retire Candidates and Verify Formula Usage exclude all fields inside the grace period.
